title: Feature Request: Add UI toggle to disable auto-updates
body:
## Feature Request

Currently, Claude Island uses Sparkle for auto-updates with `SUEnableAutomaticChecks` enabled by default. While auto-updates are convenient, some users may prefer to review updates manually before installing them, especially from a security perspective (supply chain attack mitigation).

### Current Situation

- Auto-updates are enabled by default
- The app menu only shows "Check for Updates" option
- No Preferences/Settings UI is available
- The only way to disable auto-updates is via command line:
  ```bash
  defaults write com.celestial.ClaudeIsland SUEnableAutomaticChecks -bool false
  ```

### Proposed Solution

Add a simple toggle in the app's UI (either in a Preferences window or directly in the menu bar dropdown) to allow users to enable/disable automatic update checks.

This could be:
1. **Option A**: A dedicated Preferences window with update settings
2. **Option B**: A simple checkbox in the menu: "□ Check for updates automatically"
3. **Option C**: Document the `defaults` command in the README for users who want this option

### Benefits

- Better user control over updates
- Security-conscious users can review changelogs before updating
- Improved transparency around update behavior
- Standard practice in many macOS menu bar apps

### Additional Context

Even with this toggle, the "Check for Updates" menu item would still allow users to manually check for updates when they choose to.

Thanks a lot for the amazing tool and for considering this feature! :)

title: Issue: Alert sound and UI bounce incorrectly triggered on context resume
body:
## Description

When a Claude Code session runs out of context and resumes, the notification sound plays and the notch UI bounces as if a task has completed. This is incorrect behavior - the session is simply resuming with a context summary, not completing work.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run Claude Code on a task that consumes the full context window
2. When context exhausts, Claude automatically resumes with a summary message
3. **Observed:** Notification sound plays and notch bounces
4. **Expected:** No alert should trigger since no task was completed

## Root cause

The alerter in [NotchView.swift](https://github.com/MarcinusX/claude-island/blob/main/ClaudeIsland/UI/Views/NotchView.swift#L431-L484) triggers when a session enters the `waitingForInput` phase. However, context resume also sends `waiting_for_input` status via the hook, even though the assistant message is just the resume preamble:

> "This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The conversation is summarized below:"

The current code does not distinguish between:
- **Actual task completion** → should alert
- **Context resume** → should NOT alert

## Fix

PR submitted: https://github.com/farouqaldori/claude-island/pull/17

The fix filters out sessions where `lastMessage` starts with the context resume prefix before triggering the sound and bounce animation.

title: feat: Allow configuring Auto screen priority (main vs built-in)
body: ## Problem When using Claude Island with a multi-monitor setup where an external display is the primary/main display, the current "Automatic" screen selection always prioritizes the built-in display over the main display. This makes sense for users who want Claude Island on their notched MacBook display, but for users who are typically docked in front of a larger external monitor, it means manually selecting the specific display rather than relying on Auto. My setup: - MacBook Pro (with notch) on a stand behind my desk - Dell U3224KB as primary display and dock - Dell U2717D as ternary display - "Displays have separate Spaces" disabled (as recommended by tiling window managers like AeroSpace) In this configuration, the menu bar only appears on the primary display, and the top region of the built-in display becomes a "dead zone" where clicks trigger Mission Control. I'd prefer Claude Island to live on my primary display where the menu bar is active. ## Proposed Solution Add a user-configurable priority setting for Automatic mode: - **Prefer main display** — `NSScreen.main ?? NSScreen.builtin` - **Prefer built-in display** — `NSScreen.builtin ?? NSScreen.main` (current behaviour) This could be implemented as nested sub-options that appear when "Automatic" is selected: ``` Screen Auto ▾ ● Automatic ✓ Main, then built-in ● Prefer main display ○ Prefer built-in display ○ DELL U3224KB ○ Built-in Retina Display ``` The sublabel under "Automatic" would update dynamically to reflect the current priority ("Main, then built-in" or "Built-in, then main"). ## Why Both Options Matter - **Prefer built-in** makes sense for users who want Claude Island on their notched display, which is the original design intent - **Prefer main** makes sense for users who are docked with an external primary display and want Claude Island to follow their focus With this approach, Auto becomes truly automatic for both use cases: - When I'm docked at home, Auto selects my Dell (main) - When I'm on the road, Auto selects my built-in display (fallback) ## Implementation I've prototyped this locally and would be happy to submit a PR if there's interest. title: Bug: Window expands and retracts multiple times when waking from sleep
body:
## Description

When waking the computer from sleep, the Claude Island window expands and retracts 2-3 times with approximately 1 second intervals. This is a visual annoyance but doesn't affect functionality.

## Root Cause

Two issues contribute to this behaviour:

1. **No debouncing of screen change notifications**: macOS fires multiple `NSApplication.didChangeScreenParametersNotification` events in rapid succession as displays reconnect after wake. Each notification triggers window recreation.

2. **Boot animation on every window recreation**: The window performs an expand/retract "boot animation" every time it's recreated, not just on initial app launch.

3. **Unnecessary recreation**: The window is recreated even when the screen configuration hasn't actually changed.

## Expected Behaviour

When waking from sleep, the window should remain stable without any visible expand/retract cycles (assuming the screen configuration hasn't changed).

## Environment

- macOS with external display
- Claude Island v1.2

title: fix(screen): prevent window flicker when waking from sleep

title: Bug: Archiving session doesn't terminate terminal process and breaks re-sync
body:
## Description

When archiving a session from the app, the underlying terminal Claude Code process continues running. If the user continues working in the terminal, the app no longer tracks it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the Claude Island app
2. Start a Claude Code session in terminal
3. The session appears in the app (works correctly)
4. Click the archive/close button on the session in the app
5. The session disappears from the app UI
6. **However**, the terminal session is still running
7. Continue working in the terminal session
8. Nothing appears in the app anymore

## Expected Behavior

Either:
- The app should continue tracking the session if it's still running in terminal, OR
- The app should clearly indicate that archiving only hides the session (not terminate it), OR
- The app should offer to actually terminate the session

## Actual Behavior

- Archive removes the session from UI state (`sessions.removeValue(forKey: sessionId)`)
- File watchers are cancelled for that session
- The terminal process continues running independently
- No mechanism exists to re-associate the running session with the app
- Hook events from the still-running session are effectively orphaned

## Root Cause Analysis

Looking at the code flow:

```
archiveSession() 
  → sessionMonitor.archiveSession(sessionId:)
    → SessionStore.process(.sessionEnded(sessionId:))
      → SessionStore.processSessionEnd()
        → sessions.removeValue(forKey: sessionId)  // Remove from UI state
        → cancelPendingSync(sessionId:)            // Stop file watcher
```

The archive action only cleans up the app's internal state but has no interaction with the actual Claude Code process running in the terminal.

## Suggested Fix

One of these approaches:

1. **Re-detection approach**: When a hook event arrives for an "archived" session ID, re-add it to the tracked sessions instead of ignoring it. This would allow the session to "come back" if the user continues working in terminal.

2. **Clearer UX**: Rename "Archive" to "Hide" and add a tooltip/warning that the terminal session is still running.

3. **Confirmation dialog**: When archiving, show a dialog explaining that the terminal session will continue running and ask if the user wants to just hide it or actually terminate it (if termination is implemented).

## Environment

- macOS
- Claude Island (latest)
- Claude Code CLI

title: Fix: Re-detect archived sessions when hook events continue to arrive
body:
## Summary
- Fixes the bug where archiving a session from the app breaks sync with a still-running terminal session
- When a user archives a session, the app now tracks it so it can be re-detected if hook events continue to arrive
- Automatically restarts the interrupt watcher when an archived session is re-detected

## Problem
When a user archives (closes) a session from the app, the underlying terminal Claude Code process continues running. Previously, if the user continued working in the terminal after archiving, the app would never sync again because:
1. Archive called `sessionEnded`, which removed the session entirely
2. File watchers were cancelled
3. No mechanism existed to re-associate the running session with the app

## Solution
- Added a new `sessionArchived` event that tracks archived session IDs separately from truly ended sessions
- When hook events arrive for an archived session, the app re-adds it to active sessions and restarts watchers
- True session ends (from Claude's `SessionEnd` hook) still permanently remove sessions

title: Notification sound incorrectly triggered when subagent completes
body:
## Description
The notification sound plays when a subagent (Task tool) completes, even though the main Claude session is still processing.

## Root Cause
In `claude-island-state.py`, the `SubagentStop` event sets `status="waiting_for_input"`, which triggers the notification sound. However, when a subagent completes, the main session continues processing (it receives the subagent result and keeps going) - it's not actually waiting for user input.

## Expected Behavior
- Notification sound should **only** play when the main session finishes and is waiting for user input
- Subagent completions should **not** trigger notification sounds

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a Claude session with hooks enabled
2. Have Claude spawn subagents (Task tools)
3. Notice notification sound plays each time a subagent completes

## Proposed Fix
Change `SubagentStop` to report `status="processing"` instead of `"waiting_for_input"` in `claude-island-state.py`.

## Related
Similar to #18 (context resume also incorrectly triggered sounds)

title: Add NATS-based remote session support
body:
## Summary

- Add NATS transport to the hook script so Claude Island can monitor Claude Code sessions running on remote machines via SSH
- Add a local bridge daemon (`nats-bridge.py`) that subscribes to NATS events and forwards them to Claude Island's Unix socket, with bidirectional permission approve/deny support
- Add a tmux proxy pane relay (`nats-proxy-pane.py`) for message relay from Claude Island to remote sessions via SSH

## How it works

The hook script auto-detects SSH sessions (`SSH_CLIENT`, `SSH_TTY`, `SSH_CONNECTION` env vars) and falls back to NATS when the Unix socket is unavailable. No pip dependencies needed on the remote machine — it uses raw NATS protocol over TCP.

On the local Mac, the bridge daemon:
- Forwards state events to Claude Island via Unix socket
- Handles permission request/reply (300s timeout)
- Writes `.jsonl` transcripts for remote sessions
- Manages tmux proxy panes per session (resolves SSH aliases from `~/.ssh/config`)

**Prerequisite:** NATS server on local Mac + SSH `RemoteForward 4222 localhost:4222`

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `ClaudeIsland/Resources/claude-island-state.py` | Add `is_remote()`, `nats_publish()`, `nats_request()`, `get_remote_tmux_target()`, `get_remote_hostname()`, modified `send_event()` and `PermissionRequest` handler, added `user_prompt`/`last_assistant_message`/`remote_tmux_target`/`remote_hostname` to state |
| `scripts/remote/nats-bridge.py` | New — local bridge daemon |
| `scripts/remote/nats-proxy-pane.py` | New — proxy pane relay |
| `scripts/remote/README.md` | New — setup docs with architecture diagram |
| `README.md` | Add remote sessions section |

## Test plan

- [x] Test remote session with NATS server + SSH RemoteForward

title: fix: Harden socket security and add hook installation consent
body:
## Summary                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
- Moves the Unix domain socket from world-accessible /tmp/ to the user-scoped ~/.claude/ directory                                                                                                                                                                           
- Adds token-based authentication to prevent unauthorized processes from sending events to the app                                                                                                                                                                           
- Restricts socket file permissions from 0o777 to 0o600 (owner-only)                                                                                                                                                                                                         
- Adds a first-launch consent dialog before installing hooks into the user's Claude Code configuration                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
## Changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
- HookSocketServer.swift: Move socket path from /tmp/claude-island.sock to ~/.claude/claude-island.sock; generate a random auth token on server start, write it to ~/.claude/hooks/.claude-island-token with 0o600 permissions; validate the token on every incoming       
  connection and reject unauthorized events; clean up legacy /tmp/ socket on start; add token field to HookEvent
- claude-island-state.py: Update socket path to ~/.claude/claude-island.sock; read auth token from ~/.claude/hooks/.claude-island-token and include it in every event sent to the app
- Settings.swift: Add hooksConsentGiven setting (tri-state: nil = never asked, true = consented, false = declined)
- AppDelegate.swift: Replace direct HookInstaller.installIfNeeded() call with installHooksWithConsent() that checks consent state, grants implied consent to existing users who already have hooks installed, and shows a consent dialog for new users
- NotchMenuView.swift: Sync the hooks toggle in the settings menu with the consent state

## Security considerations

- The previous socket at /tmp/claude-island.sock with 0o777 permissions allowed any process on the system to send events, potentially injecting fake permission approvals
- The new location under ~/.claude/ with 0o600 permissions restricts access to the current user
- The token authentication adds defense in depth: even if another process can access the socket, it cannot send valid events without reading the token file (also 0o600)
- The consent dialog ensures hooks are not silently installed into the user's Claude Code configuration on first launch

title: Add global keyboard shortcuts for approve/deny permissions
body:
## Context

Hey! Love this project — the Dynamic Island UX for Claude Code is brilliant. I kept finding myself reaching for keyboard shortcuts to approve/deny permissions without having to mouse up to the notch, especially during fast iteration loops. So I put together this feature as a suggestion.

**These are proposed changes only** — I don't have any permissions on this repo. Happy for you to take, adapt, cherry-pick, or ignore any of this. Just wanted to share what worked well for me and a colleague.

## What this adds

System-wide keyboard shortcuts for approving/denying Claude Code permission requests, plus several UX improvements to the notch behavior around permissions.

### Keyboard shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **⌘⇧Y** | Approve the selected pending permission |
| **⌘⇧N** | Deny the selected pending permission |
| **⌘⇧↑** | Cycle selection to previous pending session |
| **⌘⇧↓** | Cycle selection to next pending session |

- Shortcuts work **globally** from any app — uses Carbon `RegisterEventHotKey`, no Accessibility permission required
- Shortcuts are **configurable** via a new "Keyboard Shortcuts" row in the settings menu, with a shortcut recorder UI
- Can be enabled/disabled from settings

### Multi-session approval selection

When multiple Claude sessions have pending permission requests simultaneously:

- An **amber accent bar** on the left edge of the row indicates which session the shortcut will act on
- **⌘⇧↑ / ⌘⇧↓** cycles between pending sessions (wraps around)
- First pending session is auto-selected by default
- Selection auto-reconciles when sessions resolve or new ones arrive
- A **count badge** (e.g. "2") appears on the closed notch when 2+ sessions need approval

### Notch behavior improvements

- **Always expands for permissions** — removed the `TerminalVisibilityDetector` check that suppressed expansion when a terminal was visible. Users need to see what tool is requesting approval.
- **Persistent while pending** — clicking outside the notch no longer dismisses it when there are unanswered permission requests. Clicks still pass through to the underlying app.
- **Auto-retracts when done** — after all permissions are resolved, the notch closes automatically (0.8s for shortcut-triggered, 5s for manually-opened). Only applies when showing the instances list, not when user is in chat or menu.
- **Dynamic sizing** — instances list height scales to content (~52pt per row) instead of a fixed 320pt, clamped between 120-400pt.

## Design decisions

- **Carbon `RegisterEventHotKey`** over `NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents(.keyDown)` — the latter doesn't reliably fire for keyboard events when the app isn't focused. Carbon hotkeys are the proper macOS API for this and don't require Accessibility permission.
- **`KeyCombo` model** is `Codable` and persisted via `UserDefaults` (through `AppSettings`) so custom bindings survive app restarts.
- **Selection state lives on `NotchViewModel`** — it's UI state, not session state, and needs to be accessible from both SwiftUI views and the shortcut handler.
- **Sorted approval IDs** in the cycling logic match the visual sort order in `ClaudeInstancesView` so what the user sees matches what they cycle through.

## Files changed

### New files (3)

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Models/KeyboardShortcut.swift` | `KeyCombo` model — key code + modifier flags, `Codable`, human-readable `displayString` (e.g. "⌘⇧Y"), full Carbon key code → string mapping |
| `Services/Shortcuts/KeyboardShortcutHandler.swift` | Singleton that registers Carbon hotkeys, routes events to approve/deny/cycle handlers, selection-aware targeting |
| `UI/Components/ShortcutSettingsRow.swift` | Expandable settings row with enable/disable toggle, shortcut recorder for each binding, reset to defaults |

### Modified files (5)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `Core/Settings.swift` | Added `shortcutsEnabled`, `approveShortcut`, `denyShortcut` to `AppSettings` with `UserDefaults` persistence |
| `Core/NotchViewModel.swift` | Added `selectedPendingSessionId`, `hasPendingPermissions`, `reconcilePendingSelection()`, `cyclePendingSelection()`, dynamic `instanceCount`-based sizing |
| `UI/Views/NotchView.swift` | Wired shortcut handler startup, selection reconciliation in `onChange`, count badge in closed header, auto-retract timers, always-expand for permissions |
| `UI/Views/NotchMenuView.swift` | Added `ShortcutSettingsRow()` to the appearance settings section |
| `UI/Views/ClaudeInstancesView.swift` | Added `isSelected` parameter to `InstanceRow`, renders amber left accent bar when selected + waiting for approval |

## Testing done

Tested manually on macOS 15.6, MacBook Pro with notch:

- [x] Single permission request — ⌘⇧Y approves from another app
- [x] Single permission request — ⌘⇧N denies from another app
- [x] Two concurrent permission requests — ⌘⇧↑/↓ cycles selection, accent bar moves
- [x] Approve selected session — remaining session auto-selects
- [x] Notch stays open on click-away while permissions pending
- [x] Notch auto-retracts after all permissions resolved
- [x] Custom shortcut recording in settings
- [x] Dynamic notch height with 1 vs multiple sessions
- [x] Count badge shows on closed notch with 2+ pending

## Screenshots

_(Built and tested locally — happy to provide screenshots/recordings if helpful)_

---

Thanks again for building Claude Island — it's become part of my daily workflow. Let me know if you have any questions about the implementation or want me to adjust anything.

title: Chat view only shows tool calls, not user/assistant messages
body:
## Description

The chat history view shows tool calls and permission requests correctly, but **user and assistant text messages are not displayed**. The chat appears mostly empty despite active conversations.

## Root cause

The chat history is read from JSONL conversation files via `ConversationParser`, which looks for files at a hardcoded path:

```swift
NSHomeDirectory() + "/.claude/projects/" + projectDir + "/" + sessionId + ".jsonl"
```

Users who have configured a custom Claude config directory (e.g. `~/.claude-work/` instead of `~/.claude/`) will have their JSONL files in a different location. The app finds no conversation data and silently shows an empty chat — while hook-based events (tool calls, permissions) still work because they come through the Unix socket, not from the JSONL files.

## Workaround

Symlinking `~/.claude/projects` → `~/.claude-work/projects` (or wherever the real projects dir lives) makes it work.

## Suggested fix

Instead of hardcoding `~/.claude/`, the app should resolve the Claude config directory dynamically. Options:

1. Read the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable (if Claude Code supports one)
2. Derive the path from the hook event's `cwd` + process inspection
3. Allow users to configure the config directory path in the app's settings

## Environment

- macOS 26.3.1
- Claude Code running in tmux
- Claude config directory: `~/.claude-work/` (non-default)

## Problem

Chat history view shows only tool calls but no user/assistant messages when Claude Code is configured with a custom config directory (like `~/.claude-work/` instead of default `~/.claude/`).

I had same problem - my conversation view was always empty even though the session was active. Took me a while to figure out it was the hardcoded path.

## Root Cause

The app has `NSHomeDirectory() + "/.claude/projects/"` hardcoded in 4 files across 7 locations. Anyone using a non-default config directory (via `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` env var) or the new default location (`~/.config/claude/` since Claude Code v2.1.30+) gets empty conversations because the JSONL files are in a different place.

Hook-based events (tool calls, permissions) still work because they come through the Unix socket, but conversation text comes from the JSONL files which the app cant find.

## Fix

Created `ClaudeConfigDir.swift` utility that resolves the projects path dynamically:

1. Check `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable (user override)
2. Check `~/.config/claude/projects/` (new default since v2.1.30+)
3. Fall back to `~/.claude/projects/` (legacy)

Returns the first path that actually contains a `projects/` subdirectory.

Then replaced all 7 hardcoded path references across 4 files:

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `ConversationParser.swift` | 4 paths replaced |
| `AgentFileWatcher.swift` | 1 path replaced |
| `JSONLInterruptWatcher.swift` | 1 path replaced |
| `AppDelegate.swift` | 1 path replaced |

## How it works now

```
Before: NSHomeDirectory() + "/.claude/projects/" + projectDir + "/"
After:  ClaudeConfigDir.projectsPath + "/" + projectDir + "/"
```

Users with custom config dirs no longer need the symlink workaround mentioned in the issue.

## Summary

Fixes 3 P0 bugs that affect core session monitoring reliability:

- **Issue #22 — Sleep/wake window bounce**: `ScreenObserver` now debounces screen-change notifications (500ms) and suppresses events for 2s after system wake, preventing the notch window from bouncing open/closed during sleep/wake cycles.
- **Issue #11 — Session detection failure**: Python hook adds 3-retry socket connection with pre-check, `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` for clean EOF, and stderr diagnostics. - **Issue #29 — Session state inconsistency**: `SessionStore.processHookEvent` reorders operations (tool tracking → phase transition → permission status). Removes duplicate `publishState()` call. Replaces recursive `process(.toolCompleted)` with inline `applyToolCompletions()` to prevent UI from seeing intermediate states.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |

title: feat(ui): enhance AI agent presentation in notch panel
body:
## Summary

Claude Island 目前對 AI agent 的呈現是「扁平列表 + 最小資訊」模式。隨著多 agent orchestration 越來越普遍（subagent spawn subagent、parallel agents、typed agents），UI 需要升級以匹配這些工作流的複雜度。

本 issue 彙整所有可改良方向，依優先級排列。

---

## P0 — Agent Type 視覺分化

**現況**：所有 subagent 只有 5px cyan/green 圓點，無法區分 executor、reviewer、planner、explorer 等不同角色。

**改善**：`TaskContext` 已有 `agentType` / `agentName` 欄位，但 UI 沒使用。應根據 agent type 顯示不同的 pixel art icon + 專屬顏色：

| agentType | 圖示概念 | 顏色 |
|-----------|---------|------|
| `executor` | 扳手/齒輪 | cyan |
| `code-reviewer` | 放大鏡 | amber |
| `planner` / `Plan` | 羅盤 | purple |
| `Explore` | 望遠鏡 | teal |
| `writer` | 羽毛筆 | green |
| `verifier` | 盾牌 | emerald |
| `general-purpose` | 星星 | white-dim |

**涉及檔案**：`ClaudeInstancesView.swift` (subagentSection)、新增 `PixelAgentTypeIcon.swift`

---

## P0 — Task 進度環 (Progress Ring)

**現況**：`Tasks (3 done, 1 in progress, 2 open)` 是純文字，掃視效率低。

**改善**：用 12-14px 圓環取代文字 header，三色弧段表示 done/in-progress/pending 比例，旁邊顯示 `4/7`。一眼掌握完成度。

**涉及檔案**：`ClaudeInstancesView.swift` (taskSection)、新增 `MiniProgressRing.swift`

---

## P1 — Activity Sparkline

**現況**：看不出 agent 的活躍程度，只有靜態 duration 字串。

**改善**：在 instance row 右側加 ~60x12px 的 sparkline，基於 tool call 時間戳畫出最近 5 分鐘的活動密度（每格 15 秒，亮度 = tool call 數量）。同時跑多個 session 時，一眼分辨誰在猛幹活、誰在等待。

**涉及檔案**：`ClaudeInstancesView.swift`、新增 `ActivitySparkline.swift`、`SessionState.swift`（需記錄 tool call timestamps）

---

## P1 — Tool Activity Stream

**現況**：subagent 只顯示最後一個 running tool，看不到連續操作脈絡。

**改善**：顯示最近 3-5 個 tool calls 的 compact stream，用 opacity 遞減讓舊的漸淡：

```
  $ npm install express              ✓
  Edit: src/server.ts:42             ✓
  Write: src/routes/auth.ts          ✓
  $ npm test                         ● running
```

**涉及檔案**：`ClaudeInstancesView.swift` (subagentSection)

---

## P1 — Closed Notch Agent 概覽

**現況**：Closed notch 只顯示一個 session 的最後訊息 + spinner，浪費空間。

**改善**：加 mini agent dashboard strip — 小圓點陣列代表各 session 狀態（顏色區分 processing/waiting/idle），可選的 mini progress bar 代表 aggregate task 完成度。不用打開就知道整體狀態。

**涉及檔案**：`NotchHeaderView.swift`、`NotchViewModel.swift`

---

## P2 — Subagent 層級樹狀呈現

**現況**：多層 subagent 全部 flatten 成一層，看不出 parent-child 關係。

**改善**：用縮排 + 連接線呈現層級：

```
├─ 🔧 executor "Implement auth"        2m14s
│  ├─ 🔍 reviewer "Review changes"     Done
│  └─ 🔧 executor "Fix tests"          45s
└─ 📡 explorer "Research API"           1m03s
```

**涉及檔案**：`SessionState.swift`（`TaskContext` 需新增 `parentTaskId`）、`SubagentState`、`ClaudeInstancesView.swift`

---

## P2 — Phase Timeline Ribbon

**現況**：看不出 session 經歷過什麼狀態變化。

**改善**：在 instance row 底部加 2-3px 高的彩色條帶，每段顏色代表一個歷史 phase（cyan=processing, amber=waiting, green=done）。極 compact 但資訊豐富。

**需要**：`SessionState` 新增 `phaseHistory: [(SessionPhase, Date)]` 記錄狀態轉換。

**涉及檔案**：`SessionState.swift`、`SessionStore.swift`、`ClaudeInstancesView.swift`、新增 `PhaseRibbon.swift`

---

## P3 — Dashboard Grid Mode

**現況**：4-5+ 個 session 時需要 scroll long list。

**改善**：當 session ≥ 4 時可切換為 grid/tile mode，每個 tile 是 condensed card（creature icon + 狀態 + 進度 + agent count）。

---

## P3 — StatsHeaderBar 增強

**現況**：Header 只有 3 個 dot counts。

**改善**：加入 aggregate subagent count 和 aggregate task progress：
```
●3 processing  ●2 waiting  ●1 idle  │  ⌥7 agents  ☑12/20 tasks
```

---

## 附帶：現有 Code 可順手修的 SwiftUI Issues

- [ ] `foregroundColor()` → `foregroundStyle()`（deprecated，多處）
- [ ] `cornerRadius()` → `clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius:))`（deprecated，多處）
- [ ] `showsIndicators: false` → `.scrollIndicators(.hidden)`
- [ ] `sortedInstances` 在 `body` 中每次重算 — 可快取
- [ ] 考慮 `@ObservedObject` → `@Observable` 遷移（macOS 14+）

---

## Implementation Order

| Phase | Items | Effort |
|-------|-------|--------|
| Phase 1 | Agent Type Icon + Progress Ring | ~1 day |
| Phase 2 | Activity Sparkline + Tool Stream + Closed Notch HUD | ~2 days |
| Phase 3 | Agent Tree + Phase Ribbon | ~2 days |
| Phase 4 | Grid Mode + Header Enhancement | ~1 day |
| Ongoing | Deprecated API cleanup | sprinkle across phases |

title: Phase 2: Split AIAgentProtocol into runtime-specific adapter protocols
body:
## Summary

- Completes Phase 2 of the event bus refactor: replaces the monolithic `AIAgentProtocol` with a layered, plane-oriented runtime adapter architecture
- `AIAgentProtocol.swift` grew from ~1,500 lines to ~1,800 lines as it became the canonical home for all protocol definitions, adapter implementations, command execution, and orchestration logic
- `AgentRegistry` was surgically refactored to metadata-only (descriptor lookup / display name resolution), removing all runtime composition responsibilities

## What Changed

### New Protocol Layer (`AIAgentProtocol.swift`)

Seven `Sendable`-compatible protocols define orthogonal runtime concerns:

| Protocol | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `RuntimeAdapter` | Entry point — exposes `descriptor` + `makePlanes()` |
| `RuntimeObservationPlane` | Filters hook events by agent ID |
| `RuntimeRecoveryPlane` | Refreshes projection state |
| `RuntimeControlPlane` | Registers canonical command handlers |
| `RuntimeCapabilityPlane` | Returns `AdapterCapabilitySnapshot` by ingress mode |
| `RuntimeSemanticPlane` | Builds `ProjectedPromptState` from hook events |
| `RuntimeSessionDiscoveryPlane` | Discovers running sessions via process tree |

A `RuntimeAdapterPlanes` struct bundles all six planes. Each concrete adapter (`ClaudeCodeRuntimeAdapter`, `CodexCLIRuntimeAdapter`, `CodexAppRuntimeAdapter`, `GeminiCLIRuntimeAdapter`, `OpencodeRuntimeAdapter`) conforms to whichever subset of planes it supports.

`RuntimeAdapterDescriptor` (a simple struct, not a protocol) carries metadata: `adapterID`, `familyID`, `legacyAgentID`, display names, priority, supported events, and `eventSourceMode`.

### RuntimeOrchestrator

`RuntimeOrchestrator` is the sole composition boundary. It owns:
- The canonical `CommandRouter` (for `approval.resolve`, `choice.submit`, `session.focus/archive/interrupt/clear`)
- All five adapter instances
- Interaction timeout lifecycle (registration, cancellation, terminal-expired emission)
- Capability refresh on mode switch

### Canonical Command Execution

`RuntimeCommandExecutor` handles dispatch: approval resolve → hook socket write-back, choice submit → hook socket write-back, session focus → yabai/tmux/NSRunningApplication activation, session interrupt/clear → tmux or tty payload injection.

### AgentRegistry (Refactored)

Now a `@MainActor ObservableObject` with a `Published descriptors` dictionary and helper methods for display-name resolution. All descriptor registration is static, driven by the adapter list.

### HookInstallableAgent Protocol

Expanded with `HookInstallSupport` utilities for safe hook install/uninstall: strips Vibe Island managed hooks from existing config, validates contract (declared events == installed events), auto-detects `python3` path.

### Phase 1 Infrastructure (present in branch, merged in prior PR)

- `CanonicalEventEnvelope` — 11 canonical event types with full round-trip Codable
- `CanonicalCommandEnvelope` — 6 canonical command types
- `CanonicalEventBus` — append-only, deduping event bus with AsyncStream fan-out
- `CommandRouter` — adapter-ID-keyed command dispatch
- `FeatureFlags` — env-var + UserDefaults gated feature flags per adapter path
- `RuntimeIdentity` — `RuntimeAdapterID` / `RuntimeFamilyID` / `RuntimeModeHint` enum trio
- `AdapterCapabilitySnapshot` / `CanonicalSemanticArea` — capability matrix

### Projection Store

- `ProjectionBootstrap` — ~1,400 lines, wires session projection from hook + process-tree signals
- `SessionProjectionStore` — ~900 lines, manages live projected session state
- `ProjectedUIStateStore` — ~460 lines, drives SwiftUI UI state
- `CompatibilityStateProjector` — backward-compat projection helpers

### New Test Coverage

- `ArchitectureInvariantTests` — 1,000+ lines verifying architecture contracts (raw payload preservation, deduping, command routing, plane composition)
- `CanonicalFoundationTests` — 850+ lines verifying all canonical schemas round-trip
- `CanonicalFixtures` — shared test fixtures for all event and command types
- `ClaudeIslandUITests` — 380+ lines of UI integration tests

## Key Architectural Decisions

1. All protocols are `Sendable` — Swift concurrency-safe by construction
2. `codex-cli` and `codex-app` are structurally distinct (separate `RuntimeAdapterID` values) — never collapsed back
3. All routing keys are `adapter_id` — `family_id` is UI grouping only
4. Feature flags gate all adapter paths — existing behavior is preserved until later phases explicitly cut over
5. `HookSocketServer` is the primary interaction response path — tty/tmux are terminal-control fallbacks

## Test Plan

- [x] `xcodebuild test -scheme ClaudeIsland -destination 'platform=macOS'` passes (unit + canonical foundation tests)
- [ ] `xcodebuild test -scheme ClaudeIsland -destination 'platform=macOS' -uiTesting YES` passes (UI tests)
- [ ] Manual smoke test: launch Claude Island, verify no regression in NotchView / ChatView / ClaudeInstancesView rendering

## Breaking Changes

None. This is an additive refactor. All feature flags default to `false`, preserving the legacy code path until individual adapter phases opt in.

title: Fix 8 bugs: security, correctness, and performance issues
body:
## Summary

Found and fixed 8 bugs across Swift, shell scripts during a thorough code review:

### Security
- **HookSocketServer.swift**: Unix domain socket created with `0o777` (world-writable) — any process could send forged hook events including fake permission approvals. Changed to `0o600` (owner-only).

### Correctness
- **MCPToolFormatter.swift**: `Bool` check was unreachable — `as? NSNumber` matches before `as? Bool`, so boolean values were formatted as `"1"/"0"` instead of `"true"/"false"`. Swapped check order.
- **ToolResultData.swift**: `GenericResult.==` only compared `rawContent`, ignoring `rawData`. SwiftUI could miss state changes when only `rawData` differed. Added `rawData` comparison via `NSDictionary.isEqual(to:)`.
- **ChatMessage.swift**: `MessageBlock.id` used `hashValue` which is randomized per process launch in Swift 4.2+, causing unstable IDs and potential UI flickering across app restarts. Replaced with deterministic SHA256-based hash.
- **generate-keys.sh**: `generate_keys` was called twice — first to capture public key, second to export private key. The second call generated a **new** key pair, so the public key (printed to terminal for Info.plist) and the exported private key were from different pairs. Fixed by using `-p` flag on the first call. Also added `chmod 600/700` on private key and directory.
- **create-release.sh**: `cat >` completely overwrote `src/config.ts`, destroying any other exports in the file. Changed to use `sed` for in-place updates when file exists.

### Performance
- **ConversationParser.swift**: `ISO8601DateFormatter` was created per message line (~2μs each, expensive). For JSONL files with hundreds of lines, this was significant. Extracted to a reusable static property.

### Build Reliability
- **build.sh**: Added `set -o pipefail` so xcodebuild failures propagate through `xcpretty` pipe. Improved fallback pattern to show full build output on failure instead of silently retrying.

body:
## Summary

Adds comprehensive usage monitoring for users with multiple Claude Code profiles (e.g., separate home/work accounts with different subscription plans).

- **Profile-aware session grouping** — sessions are split by profile in the instances list via a `--profile` flag in the hook script
- **Real-time usage limit bars** — session (5h) and weekly (7d) utilization from Anthropic's `rate_limits` API, sourced via Claude Code's status line system. No guessing at limits — uses the actual percentages from Anthropic's backend
- **Cost estimation** — per-session API cost calculated from JSONL conversation logs with per-model pricing and message deduplication
- **Burn rate** — tokens/min display
- **Lifetime savings** — total API cost vs subscription fees since account creation
- **Daily/monthly cost history** — expandable section in the settings menu
- **Plan auto-detection** — reads subscription type and rate limit tier from macOS Keychain (`Claude Code-credentials-*` entries). Two-pass keychain query: finds matching services first (attributes only), then fetches credential data only for Claude Code entries
- **Configurable display** — toggles for cost, burn rate, savings, lifetime savings, and individual limit bars. Per-profile plan override in settings
- **Scrollable settings menu** — prevents overflow when multiple sections are expanded

## Architecture

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Models/UsageModels.swift` | Data types: plans, pricing, limits, costs, display config |
| `Services/State/UsageTracker.swift` | Actor for JSONL parsing, rate limit state reading, cost calculation |
| `Services/Hooks/PlanDetector.swift` | Keychain + `.claude.json` plan auto-detection |
| `Core/UsageSettings.swift` | `@MainActor ObservableObject` for display preferences and plan config |
| `UI/Components/UsageSettingsRow.swift` | Settings toggles + per-profile plan picker |

```json
{
  "statusLine": {
    "type": "command",
    "command": "CLAUDE_ISLAND_PROFILE=home /path/to/claude-island-statusline.sh"
  }
}
```

The hook script also needs `--profile <name>` added to the command.

title: fix: resolve LazyVStack CPU thrashing (100% CPU / 48s unresponsive)
body:
## Problem

Claude Island occasionally consumes 100% CPU and becomes unresponsive for up to 48 seconds. macOS generates `cpu_resource.diag` reports pointing to layout thrashing in SwiftUI's `LazyVStack`:

```
CPU: 90 seconds cpu time over 90 seconds (100% cpu average)
process was unresponsive for 48 seconds before sampling
```

**Heaviest stack trace:**
```
LazySubviewPlacements.updateValue()
  → LazyLayoutViewCache.commitPlacedSubviews()
    → _LazyLayoutViewCache.initialPlacement() / finalPlacement()
```

## Root Cause

Three issues combine to create a layout thrashing feedback loop inside the `LazyVStack`:

### 1. `.animation(value: history.count)` on the LazyVStack (ChatView.swift:307)

During streaming, every new message increments `history.count`, which triggers a spring animation on the **entire** `LazyVStack`. This forces SwiftUI to recalculate the layout of all visible cells mid-animation. Since streaming adds messages rapidly, animations pile up and the layout engine can never settle.

### 2. Timer-driven `ProcessingIndicatorView` (ChatView.swift:652)

A `Timer.publish(every: 0.4)` updates `@State var dotCount` to cycle "Processing.", "Processing..", "Processing...". Each state mutation triggers a view update **inside** the already-thrashing `LazyVStack`, compounding the layout invalidation.

### 3. Timer-driven spinner in `InstanceRow` (ClaudeInstancesView.swift:135)

A `Timer.publish(every: 0.15)` updates `@State var spinnerPhase` to cycle through 6 symbol characters. At 6.7 updates/second **per row**, with multiple active sessions, this generates constant layout invalidation in the instances `LazyVStack`.

**Secondary issue:** `sortedInstances` produces unstable ordering when two sessions have the same priority and date, causing the `LazyVStack` to unnecessarily shuffle items.

## Fix

### ChatView.swift

| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| Remove `.animation(value: history.count)` | This was the primary thrashing trigger. The `.animation(value: isProcessing)` modifier already handles the only transition that needs animation (processing indicator appear/disappear). Individual message insertion is handled by the per-item `.transition()` modifiers. |
| Replace timer-driven dot animation with opacity-based animation | Instead of mutating `dotCount` via `Timer`, use three `Text(".")` views with staggered `.opacity` animations via `.repeatForever()`. This produces the same visual effect but uses Core Animation (GPU-composited) with zero state mutations. |

### ClaudeInstancesView.swift

| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| Replace `Timer.publish(every: 0.15)` spinner with `.rotationEffect` animation | Uses a single `✳` character with `.linear(duration: 1.0).repeatForever()` rotation. Same visual feel, zero state updates. Removes the `Combine` import entirely. |
| Add tertiary sort key (`sessionId`) | When two sessions have the same priority and date, the sort was non-deterministic, causing `LazyVStack` to see items "move" and invalidate its layout cache. `sessionId` is immutable and unique, making the sort stable. |

## Testing

1. Open Claude Island with 2+ active Claude Code sessions
2. Have at least one session actively streaming a response
3. Monitor CPU in Activity Monitor — should stay well below 50%
4. Previously this scenario would spike to 100% within ~90 seconds

body:
## Summary

When Claude Code invokes Bash with `run_in_background: true` (e.g. starting a local dev server) and then immediately ends its turn, the notch stays stuck showing **Processing...** even though Claude is actually idle and waiting for user input.

The root cause is a race between the `Stop` hook and the late-arriving `PostToolUse` hook for the backgrounded Bash. `PostToolUse` is mapped to `status="processing"`, and the SessionPhase state machine allows `.waitingForInput → .processing`, so the late `PostToolUse` flips an already-correct `.waitingForInput` back to `.processing`.

## Environment

- macOS 15.x (Darwin 25.4.0)
- Vibe Notch v1.3 (built from `main`)
- Claude Code 2.x (`claude --version` ≥ 2.1)
- Hook script: `~/.claude/hooks/claude-island-state.py` (auto-installed)

## Reproduction

1. Run any Claude Code session with vibe-notch attached.
2. Ask Claude to do something that ends with starting a backgrounded shell, e.g. `sleep 60` with `run_in_background: true`, or `python -m http.server` in the background.
3. Claude finishes its turn and the notch should turn green ("Ready for input"). Instead it stays cyan ("Processing...") indefinitely until the next `PreToolUse` arrives — which never happens because Claude is idle.

## Diagnostic evidence

Captured live via:

```bash
log stream --predicate 'subsystem == "com.claudeisland"' --info --debug --style compact
```

Real hook arrival order from a reproduction (session `8bbb736d`, all events on the same session):

```
13:28:44.729  [Hooks] Received: PreToolUse  for 8bbb736d
13:28:46.253  [Hooks] Received: Stop        for 8bbb736d   ← turn ended
13:28:47.365  [Hooks] Received: PostToolUse for 8bbb736d   ← arrives 1.1s AFTER Stop
```

The `Stop → PostToolUse` ordering is reproducible: `run_in_background:true` Bash measured a consistent ~2s gap between PreToolUse and PostToolUse in my logs (`13:27:58.902 PreToolUse → 13:28:01.019 PostToolUse`). When Claude finishes its assistant turn during that gap, `Stop` fires first.

## Root cause (file:line)

Three pieces interact:

1. `ClaudeIsland/Resources/claude-island-state.py:113` — `PostToolUse` is mapped to `state["status"] = "processing"`.
2. `ClaudeIsland/Models/SessionEvent.swift:151-162` — `determinePhase()` maps `"processing"` to `.processing`.
3. `ClaudeIsland/Models/SessionPhase.swift:117` — the state machine **allows** `.waitingForInput → .processing` (intended for "user replied, Claude resumes work" path, but it also fires on the late PostToolUse).

So `Stop` correctly transitions to `.waitingForInput`, then the delayed `PostToolUse` legally re-transitions to `.processing` and the notch never recovers until the next user prompt.

## Proposed fix

Narrow the rule in `ClaudeIsland/Services/State/SessionStore.swift:150-156`: `PostToolUse` / `PostToolUseFailure` should only be allowed to flip the session phase when we're recovering from `.waitingForApproval` (terminal-side approve, which doesn't go through the socket). In all other cases they should only update tool status, not the session phase.

```swift
// Before
let newPhase = event.determinePhase()
if session.phase.canTransition(to: newPhase) {
    session.phase = newPhase
}

// After
let newPhase = event.determinePhase()
let allowPhaseChange: Bool = {
    if event.event == "PostToolUse" || event.event == "PostToolUseFailure" {
        // PostToolUse can race after Stop for run_in_background bash.
        // Only flip phase if recovering from terminal-approved permission.
        return session.phase.isWaitingForApproval
    }
    return true
}()
if allowPhaseChange, session.phase.canTransition(to: newPhase) {
    session.phase = newPhase
}
```

## Scenario matrix

| Scenario | Behavior after fix |
|---|---|
| Normal turn (Pre→Post→Stop) | Pre→.processing, Post→no-op phase, Stop→.waitingForInput ✅ |
| Multiple sequential tools | Pre→Post(no-op)→Pre→Post(no-op)→Stop→.waitingForInput ✅ |
| **bg bash, PostToolUse arrives after Stop (this bug)** | Pre→.processing, Stop→.waitingForInput, **Post no-op** ✅ |
| Terminal-approved permission (no socket reply) | PermissionRequest→.waitingForApproval, Post sees `.waitingForApproval`→flips to .processing ✅ (preserved) |
| User replies, Claude resumes | UserPromptSubmit→.processing via `status="processing"` path ✅ (independent of PostToolUse) |
| Permission denied then Stop | PermissionRequest→.waitingForApproval, PostToolUseFailure→.processing (recovery), Stop→.waitingForInput ✅ |

## Notes

- This is purely a vibe-notch state machine fix — no upstream Claude Code change is needed.
- I have a working patch and have verified the fix locally against the reproduction. Happy to send a PR.

title: Fix notch stuck on Processing... when run_in_background:true Bash races PostToolUse after Stop
body:
Fixes #98.

## Bug

When Claude Code invokes Bash with `run_in_background: true` (e.g. starting a local dev server) and immediately ends its turn, the `PostToolUse` hook for the backgrounded Bash arrives **after** the `Stop` hook (measured ~1s gap in real logs). See the issue for the full diagnostic trace and root-cause walkthrough (file:line).

Narrow the rule in `SessionStore.processHookEvent`: `PostToolUse` / `PostToolUseFailure` are only allowed to mutate `session.phase` when recovering from `.waitingForApproval` (the terminal-side approve path that doesn't return through the socket). In every other case the tool's status is still updated but the session phase is left alone.

```swift
let allowPhaseChange: Bool = {
    if event.event == "PostToolUse" || event.event == "PostToolUseFailure" {
```

title: Fix hook crash when subprocess C extension fails to load
body:
## Summary
- `get_tty()` in `ClaudeIsland/Resources/claude-island-state.py` calls `import subprocess` at the top of the function, outside the `try/except` block that guards the rest of it.
- On macOS, if the running Python interpreter's `_posixsubprocess` C extension can't be `dlopen`'d (in my case: a Homebrew Python build whose ad-hoc-signed `.so` files got rejected by macOS's newer Gatekeeper "provenance" library-validation check), the `ImportError` propagates straight out of `get_tty()` uncaught, crashing the whole hook for every single event instead of falling back to the `os.ttyname()` methods already implemented a few lines below.
- This means a local, environment-specific Python signing issue takes down ClaudeIsland's hook entirely (every `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`/`Stop`/etc. invocation fails), rather than just losing the "ps-based" TTY detection.

## Fix
Move `import subprocess` inside the existing `try:` block so an import failure is caught the same way a failed `ps` invocation already is, and execution falls through to the `os.ttyname()` fallback.

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced the original crash locally (`ImportError: ... library load denied by system policy` from a Homebrew python@3.14 install) and confirmed `get_tty()` raised uncaught before the fix.
- [x] After the fix, ran the hook with the same broken interpreter state and confirmed it no longer crashes and falls back to `os.ttyname()`.
- [x] Re-signed the local Python install separately (unrelated to this PR) and confirmed `subprocess` also works normally end-to-end when available.

title: Don't steal focus when the notch expands
body:
When the notch expands for anything other than a task-finished notification (permission prompt, hover, manual open) it pulls keyboard focus off whatever app you're in. Pretty jarring if you're mid-typing somewhere else and it pops open.

It comes from the `.opened` handler in `ClaudeIsland/UI/Window/NotchWindowController.swift`:

```swift
NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps: false)
notchWindow?.makeKey()
```

The notch is a non-activating `NSPanel` and its buttons already work through mouse events (`ignoresMouseEvents = false` gets set on open), so making the app active + the window key isn't needed for approve/deny to work -> it only serves to grab focus. This just drops those two lines so the notch never takes focus when it opens.

Tested locally: built Release, buttons still click fine and focus stays with the foreground app.

One thing I wasn't sure on: some people might actually want it to grab focus so they can approve/deny from the keyboard. Perhaps this should be configurable?

title: Answer AskUserQuestion prompts from the notch
body:
Adds answering of `AskUserQuestion` prompts straight from the notch, instead of forcing a trip to the terminal.

### What it does
- The notch auto-opens on a pending question and jumps to the chat view.
- Options are clickable rows; single-select submits on click, multi-select toggles and submits with a Send button.
- Answers are sent to the picker over `tmux send-keys`. Sessions not running under tmux keep the existing "go to terminal" bar.
- Picked options stay visible in the chat after the picker closes.

### Multi-select mechanics
A bare digit in the picker only *toggles* a row and leaves the cursor on the first one, so sending Return after the digits toggled option 1 instead of submitting. The cursor now walks down past every option plus the "Type something" row onto `Submit`, and the trailing "Ready to submit your answers?" review screen is confirmed once it appears in the pane. Verified against a live picker in a scratch tmux session.

Multi-select rows render a checkbox rather than a number badge, since clicking them toggles rather than submits.

### Keeping the answer in the chat
Hooks create the tool item without a payload (`PostToolUse` marks success with no result), and the JSONL merge skips ids it already knows — so the result never reached the store and the chat showed an `AskUserQuestion` row with nothing under it. Two changes:
- `ToolCallItem` carries what was sent from the notch, recorded at submit time.
- `backfillToolResults` fills in results for hook-created items when JSONL does carry them, and `processToolCompleted` no longer treats a payload-less completion as final.

Also: `AskUserQuestionResult.answers` is keyed by question text, but the view looked it up by index, so the answer never rendered even when the structured result was present. Fixed, with the index lookup kept as a fallback.

Tested on macOS with Claude Code running under tmux, single- and multi-select, including multi-question sets.

title: Fix/hook installer hardening
fix: don't let a late PostToolUse resume an idle session (#98)
body:
Fixes #98.

## Problem

When Claude Code runs a Bash tool with `run_in_background: true` and then ends its turn, the `PostToolUse` hook can arrive **after** `Stop`. `PostToolUse` maps to `status="processing"` and `SessionPhase` allows `.waitingForInput → .processing`, so the late event drags an already-idle session back into `.processing` with nothing left to move it out. `SubagentStop` has the same shape.

The session then never recovers. `startPeriodicStatusCheck` only re-syncs sessions in `.processing` or `.waitingForApproval`, so every 3s it re-reads the JSONL and republishes state — the notch stays stuck on "Processing..." and re-animates indefinitely.

Observed on a session that had been idle for ~4 hours:

```
15:34:19  [Session] Processing: fileUpdated(session: 513ab18e, messages: 18)
15:34:22  [Session] Processing: fileUpdated(session: 513ab18e, messages: 18)
15:34:25  [Session] Processing: fileUpdated(session: 513ab18e, messages: 18)
```

Same message count each time — nothing had changed on disk since 11:38. The user-visible symptom is a notch that keeps flickering while every conversation is idle.

## Fix

A turn only ever resumes on `UserPromptSubmit` (the user replied) or `PreToolUse` (Claude started a new tool). Any other event that would move `.waitingForInput → .processing` is ignored.

This is narrower than touching `SessionPhase.canTransition`, which deliberately allows that edge for the legitimate resume path — the distinction is *which event* is asking for it, and only `SessionStore` has that context. Recovery from `.waitingForApproval` (terminal-side approve, which doesn't go through the socket) is untouched: the guard only fires when the current phase is `.waitingForInput`.

## Verification

Built from this branch and run against two live Claude Code sessions on macOS 26.6 / Xcode 26.6.

Before — the 3s re-sync loop on the idle session, in `log stream --predicate 'subsystem == "com.claudeisland"' --level debug`:

```
fileUpdated(session: 513ab18e, messages: 18)   ×1 every 3s, indefinitely
```

After — the loop is gone; only real events from the active session remain:

```
[Hooks]   Received: PreToolUse for bdf4bbd1
[Session] Processing: hookReceived(PreToolUse, session: bdf4bbd1)
[Hooks]   Received: PostToolUse for bdf4bbd1
[Session] Processing: hookReceived(PostToolUse, session: bdf4bbd1)
```

Permission approve/deny and normal processing → ready transitions still behave as before.

The repo has no test target, so this ships without a test.

title: Memory leak: Vibe Notch grows to ~64 GiB overnight, freezes macOS (v1.3.2)
body:
## Summary

Vibe Notch v1.3.2 grew to about **64.5 GiB resident memory** overnight on a 64 GB Mac while the machine was idle. This exhausted system memory, caused repeated jetsam events and two WindowServer watchdog timeouts, and finally left the Mac completely frozen until it was forced off.

## Environment

- Vibe Notch 1.3.2 (build 6), installed with the Claude Code hooks (`claude-island-state.py` on all hook events, matcher `*`)
- macOS 15.7.9 (24G830)
- MacBook Pro, M3 Max (Mac15,9), 64 GB RAM
- Several Claude Code sessions open in terminal windows, machine left awake on AC overnight

## What happened (local times)

- **01:43 to 01:53**: 13 JetsamEvent reports. In every one of them Vibe Notch was the largest process, at **64.4 to 64.7 GiB** resident (`rpages` x 16 KiB). The next largest process was at 6.1 GiB. The app was already at that size at the first report, so the growth started earlier.
- **07:38 and 07:39**: two WindowServer `userspace_watchdog_timeout` reports (WindowServer unresponsive for 80 s).
- **07:39**: the unified log stops. No panic report was written. The machine stayed frozen until a forced restart hours later.

The app wrote almost nothing to the unified log overnight (only 2 `UAUserActivity` messages), so there is no app-side log explaining the growth.

## Expected

The memory used by the notch app should stay flat while sessions are idle.

## Possible lead (unverified)

The growth seems unbounded and independent of user activity. Perhaps per-session or per-event state received through `/tmp/claude-island.sock` (hook events, transcripts) is kept forever and never pruned. This is a guess, I did not inspect the source.

## Notes

I have uninstalled the app for now. I can provide anonymised excerpts of the jetsam reports if useful.

title: Fix duplicate click on panel dismiss and unbounded tool cache / parser state
body:
## What this PR changes

1. **Panel dismissal no longer synthesizes a second click.** Clicking outside the opened panel closes it, then 50 ms later re-posts a full mouseDown + mouseUp at the same point. The global monitor used to detect that outside click is read-only, so the original click already reaches the app underneath; the repost turns one click into two. In a text editor this can register as a double/triple click, changing the cursor or selection (and a following keystroke then overwrites the selected text). The dismissal click is now consumed, like a normal macOS popover.

2. **Bounds the `tool_use_id` cache.** Every `PreToolUse` cached `sessionId + toolName + the full tool_input JSON`; entries were only removed by a matching `PermissionRequest` or `SessionEnd`, so the cache grew for the lifetime of a session. `Write`/`Edit` inputs contain whole file contents, so a single key can be hundreds of KB. Entries are now dropped on `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure` and `PermissionDenied`, and the session cache is cleared on `Stop` / `StopFailure`.

3. **Releases parser state on session end.** `ConversationParser.incrementalState` kept every parsed message for every session indefinitely. It is now reset when a session ends or its process disappears.

4. **Correct coordinate conversion for the dead-zone repost.** `NSScreen.main` follows the key window and may not be the primary display, while CGEvent coordinates are relative to the primary display. The flip now uses `NSScreen.screens.first`.

## Why

The duplicate click is the most likely cause of text being unexpectedly selected or overwritten in the app behind the notch. The cache and parser growth matches the unbounded memory reported in farouqaldori/vibe-notch#112.

## Relationship to other open fixes

- Focus stealing on expand is addressed in farouqaldori/vibe-notch#105.
- Late `PostToolUse` dragging an idle session back to `processing` is addressed in farouqaldori/vibe-notch#109.
- This PR is complementary and does not touch those code paths.

## Testing

- Debug and Release builds on macOS 26.5.2 with Xcode 26.6.
- Dismissing the panel over TextEdit produces a single click; no duplicate selection change.
- Cache entries are removed after `PostToolUse`; `Stop` clears the session cache.
- Memory baseline stayed flat in a short soak (79.7 MB to 79.5 MB over one minute).

No updater/privacy changes are included; those are local-build preferences and are not proposed here.

title: Window dragging on a secondary display stops working while the notch panel is open
body:
## Summary

On a multi-monitor setup, expanding the notch panel on a secondary display makes window dragging stop working across the whole overlay area (the full-width 750 pt panel window), not just inside the visible panel. Every window on that display is affected, with any input device. Quitting Vibe Notch restores dragging immediately.

I traced it to `NotchPanel.sendEvent` / `repostMouseEvent` in `ClaudeIsland/UI/Window/NotchWindow.swift`. The re-posted CGEvent's Y coordinate is computed from `NSScreen.main.frame.height`, which is the screen containing the key window, not the primary display that defines the NSScreen coordinate origin. When the key window is on a secondary display with a different height, the re-posted event lands at the wrong Y, the intended window never receives the mouse-down, and the drag never starts.

## Environment

- Vibe Notch 1.3.2 (current appcast build)
- macOS 27.2 (26B123), Apple Silicon
- Two displays with different heights: primary 1920x1080, secondary 1600x900 arranged below the primary
- Panel configured via "specific screen" to the secondary display
- Reproduces with both a Bluetooth mouse and the built-in trackpad
- No window managers, key remappers, or global event taps installed. A head/tail `CGEventTap` differential showed identical event counts at `kCGHIDEventTap` and `kCGAnnotatedSessionEventTap`, so no other process is swallowing the events.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Connect two displays of different heights, with the secondary display below or beside the primary.
2. Configure Vibe Notch to show on the secondary display.
3. Make a normal window on the secondary display the key window (e.g. a stock TextEdit document).
4. Open the notch panel by clicking the notch.
5. Press on that window's title bar and drag. The window does not move at all. The cursor and mouse button work; only the drag fails.
6. Quit Vibe Notch and repeat. The same drag works.

The drag starts well below the visible panel, so this is not a hit-testing problem with the visible panel content; it is the full-window pass-through path.

## Observed A/B result

Using a stock TextEdit window on the secondary display, with the same start and end coordinates each time:

- Panel collapsed: the window moves (e.g. `(x, y)` -> `(x+84, y+41)`)
- Panel expanded: the window does not move at all
- Vibe Notch quit: the window moves again

## Root cause

`repostMouseEvent` converts NSScreen coordinates to CGEvent coordinates using the height of `NSScreen.main`:

```swift
private func repostMouseEvent(_ event: NSEvent, at screenLocation: NSPoint) {
    // Convert to CGEvent coordinate system (Y from top of screen)
    guard let screen = NSScreen.main else { return }
    let screenHeight = screen.frame.height
    let cgPoint = CGPoint(x: screenLocation.x, y: screenHeight - screenLocation.y)
    ...
}
```

`NSScreen.main` is the screen containing the window with keyboard focus. The NSScreen global coordinate space, however, is anchored to the primary display (the one with the menu bar). When the key window is on the secondary display, `NSScreen.main.frame.height` is the secondary display's height (900) instead of the primary display's height (1080), so the re-posted event is offset by 180 pt in Y. The re-posted mouse-down lands on the wrong window or the wrong part of the screen, so the window under the cursor never receives it and cannot start a drag.

The same problem occurs on any arrangement where the key window is not on the primary display.

## Suggested fix

Compute the Y flip against the primary display's height, not `NSScreen.main`:

```swift
// NSScreen global coordinates use the bottom-left corner of the primary display as origin.
let primaryHeight = NSScreen.screens.first?.frame.height ?? 0
let cgPoint = CGPoint(x: screenLocation.x, y: primaryHeight - screenLocation.y)
```

Equivalently, derive it from `CGDisplayBounds(CGMainDisplayID())`. It would also be safer to resolve the screen that actually contains `screenLocation` rather than assuming a single screen.

Two related robustness points:

1. `sendEvent` only re-posts `leftMouseDown/Up` and `rightMouseDown/Up`, not `leftMouseDragged` / `rightMouseDragged`.
2. `sendEvent` sets `ignoresMouseEvents = true` on pass-through and does not restore it until the panel status changes, so after the first outside click the open panel can remain non-interactive.
